phase_name: Permission Broker Foundation Policy Applicability Independent Implementation Verification
summary: Independent implementation verification of PBPA-001 v1.0 against Phase 148C.6's production implementation -- verification only, no src/pcae/** modification confirmed via git diff --name-only -- src/pcae/, empty for this phase's own changes. Reconstructed the production diff independently (git diff --numstat 88ec664a..dc56600c -- src/pcae/: exactly one file, permission_broker_foundation.py, +107/-5, matching 148C.6's own document; src/pcae/commands/push.py confirmed untouched). Compared all twelve POL-001..012 evaluate() bodies pre/post 148C.6 by direct diff inspection: byte-identical for all twelve; POL-004 (MissingHumanApprovalRule) gained only a sibling applicable_execution_classes class attribute, its evaluate() method unmodified. Independently re-derived the full PBPA-001 applicability matrix from primary source (NG-008's own condition text in docs/V0_2_EXECUTION_READINESS_NO_GO_GATES.md; the Phase 109 command-category table in docs/V0_2_PERMISSION_BROKER_COMMAND_PATH_INTEGRATION.md) rather than copying PBPA-001's own table -- all twelve rows classified EXACT against production metadata, including POL-004's {shell, backend, adapter, rollback} scope; no push-specific exemption found anywhere in the source (no action_type-conditional code inside applies_to() or applicable_execution_classes). Traced control flow confirming applicability is resolved strictly before evaluation for every rule, that applies_to() is defined exactly once (not overridden by any subclass), is a pure/deterministic/side-effect-free function of (applicable_execution_classes, execution_class) only, and that no caller-exclusion mechanism (exclude_policies or equivalent) exists anywhere in src/pcae/. Wrote and ran a new independent adversarial test suite (tests/test_phase_148c7_permission_broker_policy_applicability_independent_verification.py, 13 tests, no production file touched) attacking predicate failure (fails closed to DENY, never silently NOT_APPLICABLE), missing/duplicate canonical policy (both raise ValueError at PolicyRegistry construction), class spoofing (confirmed as contract-documented trust-boundary behavior per PBPA-REQ-032, not a defect), unknown execution class (DENY via POL-006 regardless of POL-004's harmless non-applicable resolution), mixed DENY/HUMAN_REVIEW precedence, simulation_only spoofing (applicability provably independent of simulation_only), determinism (5 repeated identical-request evaluations produce one signature), and decision-vocabulary preservation (exactly ALLOW/DENY/HUMAN_REVIEW). All 13 pass. Independently re-ran every regression suite 148C.6 claimed: broker suites (851/851 across 11 files, including the new 127-test applicability suite), push regression (84/84, 262.97s), Runtime Enforcement regression (2305/2305, 10.63s), fast_green (4391/4391, 110.31s) -- all matching 148C.6's claims exactly. Empirically re-observed (not closed) Finding B-1: a pcae push-shaped request (execution_class=mutation, approval_present=False, per PBPC-REQ-033/034/046's fixed values) now resolves POL-004 as NOT_APPLICABLE, decision ALLOW -- the original causal Foundation mechanism for B-1 appears removed, but Finding B-1 remains formally OPEN; closure requires a dedicated PBPC-001 v1.2 re-evaluation phase (148C.8), not performed here. Recorded seven Non-Blocking/Observation findings (V-1: kickoff-brief +112/-5 figure matches neither git history nor 148C.6's own +107/-5 document; V-2: POL-004's applies_to() is resolved in registry order before POL-006's structural validation runs for the same request, harmless because _compose's DENY-precedence always wins regardless, empirically confirmed; V-3: applicable_execution_classes's frozenset value is genuinely immutable but the attribute binding on a PolicyRule instance is not type-system-enforced immutable, though no public request-processing path exposes a mutable reference to a caller; V-4: 148C.6's own test-count report '851 existing + 127 new' is a labeling imprecision -- the actual pre-existing-only count is 724, not 851, so 851 is the combined total (724+127), a documentation-accuracy finding on 148C.6's artifact not a functional defect; V-5: custom/partial test registries can no longer construct without every canonical POL ID present, classified CONTRACT_REQUIRED per PBPA-REQ-073, correctly implemented; V-6: 12-hard-block centralization gap remains unresolved, unaffected by this layer; V-7: Prompt Generation remains design-only/partially_ready, unaffected by this phase), zero Blocking findings. Verified P-1 (~10 old execution_class=none/approval_present=False HUMAN_REVIEW-asserting call sites) and P-2 (test_broker_evaluated_policy_ids_always_all_twelve) planning-finding dispositions both CORRECTLY_REPLACED by direct diff inspection of 148C.6's own commit, not by trusting 148C.6's claim. Verified all four real production consumers (health.py, check.py, push.py's pcae push check observation call, task.py's pcae doctor task-memory) construct execution_class=none/approval_present=True/evidence_available=True requests, confirming zero consumer decision change across the 148C.6 implementation. Reconfirmed Prompt Generation (Phase 45A-45E) remains design-only/partially_ready against canonical evidence (docs/CAPABILITY_INVENTORY.md, PROJECT_STATUS.md's Phase 45M/45M.1/45N entries) -- recorded only as a DEFERRED STRATEGIC OBSERVATION, not implemented, not investigated further. Verdict: VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -- PBPA-001 IMPLEMENTATION CONFORMS. See docs/verification/PHASE_148C.7_PERMISSION_BROKER_FOUNDATION_POLICY_APPLICABILITY_INDEPENDENT_IMPLEMENTATION_VERIFICATION.md for full detail.
